correctness.rationale: For any nonempty finite poset, reflexive S5 triangle confluence forces each comparability component to lie in one R-class; conversely all partitions of components satisfy confluence. The \(c-1\) increasing prefix-upset probes reveal every R-class according to its maximal component index, with the last class recovered by complement. For \(q<c-1\) arbitrary persistent probes, the \((q+1)\times c\) real matrix of components not wholly included plus one all-ones row has nonzero kernel. Its positive and negative supports have identical zero-intersection statuses on every query, yielding two distinct component partitions (split versus merged) with precisely identical complete outputs. Both quantifiers and \(c=1\) boundary are accounted for. Finite checker independently exhausts discrete cases through size six for the upper bound and all smaller query families through size five, with additional non-discrete examples. These finite checks are corroboration only.

broader_coverage.reasoning: Zenger supplies the birelational S5 semantics and the comparable-world collapse, but neither the quantifier over arbitrary fixed query families nor the optimal \(q=c-1\) cost. Pawlak gives the lower-approximation operator and application notions of observability, but works in a fixed approximation space. Related finite chain-frame censuses concern different relations/axioms and do not determine this observation complexity. A general rough-set learning theorem using the same oracle could subsume the claim and remains a residual risk.

value.rationale: The exact cost of reconstructing unknown S5 indistinguishability from persistent atomic knowledge observations is a natural finite information/observability invariant. The theorem compresses arbitrary finite intuitionistic frames to their comparability-component count, supplies a universal optimal nonadaptive experiment and proves no smaller collection works even when individual probes split components. The rank argument is structural rather than a routine Boolean-chain example; the result identifies the precise observation cost of a common finite modal model class.
